# Fixed candidate type and lint diagnostics

This disabled proposal reuses the reviewed controller from publication `121f3db1362a0c4d1eb90294b8648c2719b8aa2b` and its existing workflow branch. It runs one isolated GitHub-hosted Ubuntu 24.04 job at candidate `be7b7ca8bef843177c935f43e643c870878abb2b`, tree `b37f1e1a541f8326fbde55ae61372ab75fc182dd`, ordered parents `8271986ffbad1f0fedcdb865f115488238d43858` and `dd38399e11c3babf5ea11c92fee4cedb30676e69`, from `steipete/openclaw`. Both execution flags and the job remain false for root review and activation.

The purpose is actual compiler/linter diagnostics for the three reported failing job workloads in upstream run33856860010. It is a new exact-source check, not a replay of the original test-merge checkout or a replacement for PR CI. The earlier paired comparison, dependency audit and Knip commands are not repeated. The separate full-build lifecycle proof is unchanged and is not invoked here.

## Exact native workloads

| Workload | Commands, in native order | Explicit check environment |
| --- | --- | --- |
| check-prod-types | `pnpm tsgo:prod` | `OPENCLAW_LOCAL_CHECK=0` |
| check-test-types-core-1 | `node scripts/run-tsgo-core-test-shards.mjs --stripe 1/5 --concurrency 2`, then stripe2/5 with the same arguments | none |
| check-lint-core-1 | `node --import tsx scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mts --only=core --split-core --core-stripe=1/5 --threads=1`, then `node --import tsx scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mts --only=extensions --extension-stripe=1/6 --threads=1` | `OPENCLAW_LOCAL_CHECK=0` |

The source `package.json` defines production types as core, UI and plugins joined by `&&`; this controller does not split or override that owner. Each two-command workload preserves the upstream shell's stop-on-failure barrier: type2 does not run after type1 fails, and plugin lint does not run after core lint fails. A skipped second command receives an explicit not-run verdict. Independent workloads continue after ordinary numeric failures only when source/index/lock and process closure are verified. Timeout, output overflow, integrity drift or unconfirmed cleanup stops the entire diagnostic lane.

The literal lint expansion is an explicit inference from retained metadata and exact source. The complete saved PR job matrix contains check-lint-core-1 through5. At be7, a current non-frozen hybrid PR produces only three paired core-lint jobs, while the github profile produces five; its core1 job adds plugin stripe1/6 after core1/5. This pins the workload expansion, not the original CI checkout or physical runner of every upstream job. The source contracts are `.github/workflows/ci.yml:3459,3536,3757–3791,3820–3832`; the controller's actual diagnostic runner must independently attest GitHub-hosted Ubuntu24.04. No raw Actions logs were requested or used.

The selectors remain inside the native owners. Test stripe1 covers agents-root, infra, services and packages; stripe2 covers agents-other, commands and other by the source's round-robin list. The native two-compiler limit, stop-on-first-failure within a stripe and managed child joins remain unchanged. Core lint forms its normal deterministic Program; plugin lint prepares canonical package-boundary artifacts through its existing owner. No global build is added, and no build-skipping, retry, worker, Go/heap, timeout or test-filter override is supplied.

## Preserved setup, integrity and cleanup

The controller's source/index/credential/asset/process/runtime environment/diagnostic-check functions are byte-identical to the reviewed publisher. Only source/lane/workload binding and fixed group orchestration change. The original raw-parent verification remains. All150 explicit hashes come from immutable be7 objects; the full tracked source/symlink and real index snapshots also remain mandatory. Declared hashes cover the prior134 paths plus needed current production/test type configs, script entrypoints and changed owner/caller files. Full tracked guarding covers the rest of the checkout. No source overlay is applied.

Node remains24.19.0; bundled Corepack uses the complete pnpm12.1.0 packageManager integrity pin, followed by the same `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`. Each command gets fresh private HOME/TMP/XDG/state directories and the unchanged clean CI environment. The existing diagnostic has no restored cache seeds or shared cache roots; it is not identical to a warm upstream CI worker. Native generated build/type artifacts in the one checkout may be reused between these sequential diagnostics. Actual command/source/installed-lock hashes and native outputs are retained so such limits stay inspectable. No auth, secrets, user runtime configuration or cache publication is added.

The original75-minute job ceiling and20-minute install cap remain. Production types has a900-second diagnostic cap; each paired type/lint workload shares900seconds, matching the prior paired-type diagnostic bound. Existing inner checker limits remain unchanged. Native owner timeout/output/cleanup failures are not accepted as source findings. Every command writes stdout, stderr, exit/termination/group result, source guard, canonical closure and verdict files; type-group/lint-group results preserve order and explicit skips. Overall success requires every command to pass, with no incomplete checks or cleanup errors. Normal failing checks remain red.

The inherited process owner requires leader exit and positive outer-group disappearance. Existing wrappers own nested compiler/build groups; retained dist claims and canonical cleanup errors prevent continuation. This is not an independent escaped-descendant census. Full source/real-index/stage/flag/asset/installed-lock checks run after each command and before final removal. Uncertain closure or integrity retains scratch. Artifact output remains bounded to16MiB per command and64MiB total, with8MiB per retained index/24MiB total index diagnostics. Runtime HOME/dependency/cache trees are not uploaded; existing artifact retention is14days.

No checker, compiler, linter, product, controller or dependency code was executed by this proposal lane. No Git refs, source checkout, publication checkout, GitHub or CI state was mutated. Root owns review, enabling both flags/job, manifest regeneration, publication and the subsequent interpretation of actual errors. No source fix or failure attribution is claimed before that evidence exists.
